pages.text: The shared machine screen gives different machines a common layout, but the program decides which slots are valid. Do not treat every visible inventory slot as an interchangeable input.$p$(l)Typical process inventory$()$pInputs — The labelled input area; special programs may reserve particular slots.$pOutputs — Six ordinary result slots, internally 14–19.$pPower / module — The special slot, internally 20; its role depends on the machine.$pUpgrades — Speed, Energy, Transfer and Void where supported.$pA completed batch can put results in retained overflow while normal outputs are blocked. Ordinary operation waits rather than discarding those results. The Void Upgrade is the explicit exception: it permits overflow disposal.$pAutomatic side mode follows the machine role. Input, Output and Disabled override a face. External item pipes and the Transfer Upgrade must both obey the machine automation master switch and those side modes. Energy has its own capability and direction settings.$p1. Confirm the slot label and accepted ingredient, including any analysed/stable circuit requirement.$p2. Test with no redstone signal unless the machine specifically needs one.$p3. Empty outputs and retained overflow before assuming the recipe is broken.$p4. Use Sides or the wrench to select the intended input and output faces.$p$(l:foundations_calculator:troubleshooting/automation)Automation rules and safe exports$()
